items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: early on Albert Murray had me read a book called American Humor by Constance Rourke

ctx.x: Okay. Why did you roll your eyes?

Because there’s two things that I roll my eyes at, and I roll them in great respect. I mean, and he did roll his eyes, that those kind of statements I don’t know how much good they do. I don’t know how much light they shed on anything, because well what about cartoons? What about a certain kind of cinema? What about any number of things that are uniquely American. I mean early on Albert Murray had me read a book called American Humor by Constance Rourke, it was written back around 1930 or so. And you start to see…

and part African-American and part Yankee and part Dutch and part Asian and all these kind of things. And you start to realize early on that the one and only kind of thing doesn’t really work. And the other statement that we can just get it out of the way that I also really roll my eyes at is that jazz is America’s classical music, and also jazz was America’s popular music at one time, which it never was. So those are the three oft- repeated canards, moldy canards that kind of get me going you know. But yeah.
